newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to tender for U.S. corn, wheat, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to tender for U.S. corn, wheat, soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan is expected to tender for 69,000 tonnes of wheat and up to 108,000 tonnes of soybeans and corn, all from the United States, this week, local traders said on Monday.
The Taiwan Flour Mills Association will tender on Thursday for two shipments totalling 69,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, they said.
The Taiwan Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association also plans to enter the market on Tuesday for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans, traders said.
Traders said another group may tender for a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. soybeans and corn.
Taiwanese buyers are also becoming interested in Argentine corn for April and May shipment because of the recent rise in U.S. corn futures prices.
"The recent rise in U.S. corn prices has made the Argentine corn more attractive to Taiwan buyers," a trader said.
Taiwan buyers would consider getting Argentine corn if the prices were about US$10 lower than for U.S. corn, he said.
The March corn contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was 4-3/4 U.S. cents up on Friday at $2.91-3/4 a bushel.
The local cost for Pacific Northwest freight was about $14.00 a tonne while quotes from the Gulf of Mexico ranged between $25.00-$25.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized March shipments.
Taiwan traders said Pacific Northwest freight costs could rise if damage to Zen-Noh Grain Corp's loading elevator at Convent, Louisiana, caused delays along the Mississippi river.
A ship crashed into Zen-Noh's grain elevator on Thursday, forcing a shutdown in the facility which has an annual handling capacity of 400-500 million bushels of grains and oilseeds.
Taiwan traders said they expected the elevator could be closed for up to three weeks.
Flour prices on Monday were unchanged, ranging between T$14.55 to T$15.68 a kg for Taipei delivery.
